breakdown.description: The prompt uses the polar moment J in the Euler buckling check, even though Euler buckling is governed by the flexural second moment I, not torsional rigidity.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses the second moment of area I = π d⁴/64 for the Euler buckling calculation, not the polar moment J. There is no mention of J anywhere in the output, aligning with the ground truth.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats a satisfactory average-stress yield check as if it ruled out buckling, even though a column may buckle before reaching the material yield stress.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification performs both checks independently. It notes that σ_avg is below Sy (yielding not critical), but still proceeds to evaluate Euler buckling separately, correctly identifying that P (25 kN) exceeds P_cr (≈19.3 kN) and concluding that Euler buckling is the governing limit state. It does not treat a passing yield check as sufficient to rule out buckling.
